quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: Motorcyclists must wear a helmet.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: In Illinois, wearing a helmet is not required by law. However, helmets greatly reduce the risk of head injury and are strongly recommended.

questions.question: In Illinois, which of these is allowed on a motorcycle?

options.text: A modified muffler that makes the motorcycle louder
Handlebars higher than the rider's head
A blue license plate light
A seat designed to carry two people

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat designed to carry two people
questions.explanation: In Illinois, motorcycles must have a white license plate light. You cannot modify mufflers to make them louder. Handlebars must not be higher than the rider's head. Passengers can only ride if the motorcycle and seat are designed for two people.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen by other drivers
Help you avoid road hazards
Give you a way to escape from danger
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you avoid blind spots, see better, avoid hazards, and escape danger. You should position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you
Is not worth the effort
Does not mean they will yield to you when they should
Guarantees they will yield to you

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you when they should
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but don't see them.

questions.question: An effective face shield should NOT:

options.text: Have scratches
Allow clear side views
Be airtight
Fasten securely

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?

options.text: At the front
Just behind the lead rider
At the rear

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers
Always use your headlight
Wave your arms
Ride close to vehicles in front of you

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on. Choose a lane position that gives oncoming traffic a clear view of your motorcycle. Keep space to escape if a hazard appears. Do not rely on eye contact alone to be seen.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid it
Switch lanes as quickly as possible
Stay in your lane
Flash your lights to scare the animal away

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. However, if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into other traffic is more dangerous than hitting a small animal.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible
Hold onto the seat
Put their feet on the muffler
Get on after you start the engine

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before riding. Have them get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as comfort allows and hold your waist, hips, or belt. Their feet must stay on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off the road until the rain stops
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Increase your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, depending on traffic.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead of you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the car ahead. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a penalty for a DUI conviction?

options.text: License suspension.
Installation of a breath-alcohol device in your vehicle.
A fine.
A warning.

questions.explanation: DUI penalties include license suspension, installation of a breath-alcohol device, large fines, and community service. A warning is not a typical DUI penalty.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body eliminate per hour?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. The exact time varies between people. Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you travel?

options.text: Slower than during the day under similar conditions.
At the same speed as during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than during the day under similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Travel slower at night than you would during the day. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slower speed helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, not both.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately. Do not brake while swerving. Braking while swerving may cause your motorcycle to fall over.
